issue_poll.note: Ranks 1–5 from AP VoteCast Idaho's most-important-issue question as reported (economy 37%, coronavirus 31%, health care 8%, abortion 6%, climate change 5%; other options not reported). Ranks 6–10 from national Pew 'very important' shares, skipping items already covered: Supreme Court appointments 64%, violent crime 59%, foreign policy 57%, gun policy 55%, immigration 52%. Immigration tied with race and ethnic inequality (52%); immigration chosen because Idaho's Boise State Dec 2019 survey rated it a priority (41%) and did not ask about race. caveats: Risch skipped debates and ran a slogan-heavy campaign; positions come from an Idaho Public TV forum, a newspaper questionnaire, a 2020 Senate floor release, iVoterGuide's 2020 primary profile and a 2020 Christian Coalition survey as summarized by OnTheIssues.
Immigration rated mixed: he opposed the Border Act's border funding but backed H.R.1's; the Dreamer half of his position never got a vote.

Risch's votes on S.4361, S.3386/S.3385 and H.R.1319 are inferred from party-line tallies; roll call numbers not confirmed for S.1260 (June 8, 2021) or the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act (June 23, 2022).
Only five VoteCast Idaho issues were reported; ranks 6–10 rely on national Pew data, with an immigration/racial-inequality tie broken by judgment.
